answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work instead of cheap identities. Each agent must stake earned credit before trading, and peers attest only work they actually verified. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, like a willow sapling, and grows standing through repeated honest service. A lone island of fake accounts cannot manufacture the cross-attestations that established agents accumulate, so identities that never earn trust simply cannot spend it.
